detail.longDescription: from tkinter import Tk, Toplevel, Button, Label master = Tk() def new_window(): window = Toplevel(master) #And now you can't use the master window until this window is closed Label(window, text='Hello, world!').pack() Button(master, text='Click here for a new window', command=new_window).pack() I want to make a Toplevel window that's above a Tk window. With above I mean that you can only use the Tk window when the Toplevel window is closed, just like when you add a master window to a Tkinter dialog. I know you can add a master parameter to a Toplevel (see code above) window, but you can still the use the main window. How can I cancel the main Tk window until the Toplevel window is closed?
